rationale: The Chief Justice is likely to keep the majority opinion narrow and administrable: Rule 704(b) bars only expert opinions directly about this defendant’s mental state, leaving generalized modus-operandi testimony to be policed under Rules 702/403 and instructions. A principal dissent is likely to press a text-based “functional equivalent” reading of “about whether,” with possible additional separate writing emphasizing Sandstrom-like practical effects and the jury-allocation rationale.
